title: Sri Lanka Create History As Bangladesh Suffer Record-Breaking Collapse
text:
Sri Lanka Create History As Bangladesh Suffer Record-Breaking Collapse
Bangladesh, who were cruising at 100/1 during the chase at one point, bottled the game as they went on to lose seven further wickets before they could reach 105 runs.
Sri Lanka coasted to a 77-run triumph over Bangladesh in the opening ODI of the three-match series between the sides on Wednesday as Bangladesh slumped to an unprecedented collapse during their chase at the R Premadasa Stadium in Colombo.
SL posted a total of 244 runs before bundling out Bangladesh for 167 runs in 35.5 overs as the Bangla Tigers capitulated their solid start to the chase.

Bangladesh logged an embarrassing record as they lost seven wickets for five runs, a record only second to Zimbabwe’s harrowing showing against Sri Lanka in 2008 at Harare.
Bangladesh, who were cruising at 100/1 during the chase at one point, bottled the game as they went on to lose seven wickets before they could reach 105 runs as Wanindu Hasaranga and Kamindu Mendis ran riot.
Charith Asalanka’s 106 off 123 deliveries set Sri Lanka up on steady stead after Kusal Mendis added 45 runs. Janith Liyanage, Milan Rathnayake and Hasaranga also came up with sizeable contributions for the hosts’ cause as the Lankan Lions set the tourists a target of 245 runs to win.
Bangladesh opener Parvez Hossain Emon fell for 13 off 16 to Asitha Fernando in the fifth over of the game before Tazid Hasan and Najmul Hossain Shanto steadied the chase with a 71-run stand for the secoind wicket.
However, Shanto was caught short of his crease after having added 23 runs, which initiated Bangladesh’s historic fumble.
Hasaranga removed Litton Das for a duck before dismissing Tanzid for 62 runs in the very same over. Mendis scalped Towhid Hridoy for a single run before Hasaranga returned to haunt the Bangla Tigers with the wicket of Mehidy Hasan Miraz for a duck.
Mendis doubled his tally with the removal of Tanzim Shakib before completing his three-fer with the dismissal of Taskin Ahmed for another duck to leave Bangaldesh reeling at 105/8.
Maheesh Theekshana sent Tanvir Islam back to the hut for 5 runs before Hasaranga completed the decimation of the opposition with the dismissal of Jaker Ali, who added a half-century in vain.
“Unfortunately, we had a great start, but after that, it is a tough loss for us. Seven wickets in five runs – it was unexpected," Bangladesh seamer Ahmed said.
“We tried, but it didn’t happen. Yeah, it wasn’t a great feeling," he added.
